title: An AI Search Through the Genome Turned Up a Natural Appetite Peptide
hook: Stanford scientists let an algorithm read all 20,000 human protein-coding genes looking for hidden hormones. It found a 12-amino-acid peptide that curbs appetite through the hypothalamus alone.
key_points: An algorithm called Peptide Predictor scanned all 20,000 human protein-coding genes for hormone cleavage sites.
It narrowed them to 373 candidate prohormones and 2,683 possible peptides; the team tested 100 and found BRP the most potent.
BRP is just 12 amino acids long and acts specifically in the hypothalamus, the brain's appetite and metabolism hub.
Semaglutide acts on the gut, pancreas, and other tissues too — BRP's narrower target is the point of interest.
One injection cut food intake in the next hour by up to 50% in mice and minipigs; 14 days of daily shots made obese mice lose about 3 grams, almost all fat.
Researchers saw no nausea-type responses, no change in stool output, and no major muscle loss — but this is animal work, published in Nature in March 2025.
content_html: Most hormones were found the slow way — notice an effect, chase the molecule. A Stanford Medicine team tried the reverse: build an algorithm, called Peptide Predictor, and have it read all 20,000 human protein-coding genes looking for the molecular signatures that mark a hormone precursor. That search narrowed to 373 candidate prohormones, which could in principle yield 2,683 distinct peptides. The team tested 100 of them. The standout was BRP — BRINP2-related peptide — a chain of only 12 amino acids that suppresses appetite.
extra_html:
What makes BRP interesting isn't just that it works but where. Semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic, hits receptors across the gut, pancreas, and other tissues, which is a large part of why it comes with nausea and constipation. BRP appears to act specifically in the hypothalamus, the brain's appetite-and-metabolism control center, activating a separate group of neurons. In mice and minipigs, a single injection cut food intake over the following hour by as much as 50%. Obese mice given daily injections for 14 days lost about 3 grams, with nearly all of the reduction coming from body fat, while control animals gained roughly 3 grams. The researchers reported no meaningful difference in fecal output, and did not observe the nausea-related responses or major muscle loss seen with existing drugs.

The honest caveat is the stage. This work, led by Laetitia Coassolo and Katrin Svensson, was published in Nature in March 2025 and remains animal research; human trials were planned but not yet run, and Svensson co-founded a company, Merrifield Therapeutics, to develop it. Plenty of appetite molecules have looked clean in mice and disappointed in people. What's durable here is the method — using computation to mine the genome for hormones we simply hadn't noticed.

related.title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Lower Addiction Risk
related.hook: A study of ~600,000 U.S. veterans links GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide to lower rates of addiction and overdose — an association, not proof that the drugs cause the effect.

related.title: A New Weight-Loss Pill Beats Oral Ozempic in a Major Trial
related.hook: Orforglipron, a once-daily weight-loss pill, outperformed oral semaglutide on weight loss and blood sugar in a major trial — and skips the refrigeration and meal-timing rules.

related.title: A Protein Switch That Burns Fat and Blocks New Fat Cells
related.hook: Disabling a protein nicknamed 'Mitch' boosted fat burning and blocked new fat cells from forming in human cells — and made mice leaner and more athletic.

flashcards.prompt: How did researchers find BRP in the first place?
flashcards.back_html: An algorithm called Peptide Predictor searched all 20,000 human protein-coding genes for the cleavage sites that mark a hormone precursor — narrowing to 373 candidate prohormones and 2,683 possible peptides. The team then tested 100 in the lab; BRP was the most potent.

flashcards.prompt: What distinguishes BRP's mechanism from semaglutide's?

choices.text: BRP acts specifically in the hypothalamus, while semaglutide also acts on the gut, pancreas, and other tissues
BRP works only in the stomach and never reaches the brain
BRP blocks fat absorption in the intestine

flashcards.explanation_html: BRP activates a separate group of neurons and acts specifically in the hypothalamus, the brain region governing appetite and metabolism. Semaglutide's receptors are spread across many tissues — which is part of why it brings gut side effects.

flashcards.prompt: How far along is BRP as a treatment?
flashcards.back_html: Not far. The results are in mice and minipigs, published in Nature in March 2025. Human trials are planned but hadn't begun; senior author Katrin Svensson co-founded a company to develop the molecule.
